identity.name: Dungan Revolt
native_names: 陕甘回民起义 (Shǎn-Gān Huímín Qǐyì)
alt_names: Muslim rebellion in Shaanxi and Gansu

land.text: Hui rebel centres of 1862: Xi'an (besieged by late June 1862), Jinjipu, Hezhou, Xining and Suzhou (Jiuquan)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Qing shape covers the whole of the revolt zone; this dossier adds the rebel zone on top of it.

land.text: the last Dungan towns, Urumchi and Manas, retaken in August-November 1876

successors.note: The Tarim Basin (Yettishar) and the Ili valley (Ili Sultanate) were separate rebel states with their own dossiers and ended in 1877 and 1871-1881.

rulers.name: Ma Hualong
rulers.title: fifth leader (jiaozhu) of the Jahriyya, at Jinjipu
rulers.note: Ma page: 'became the leader of the Jahriyya ca. 1849'; surrendered in January 1871; died 2 March 1871.

rulers.name: Ma Zhan'ao
rulers.title: Hui leader at Hezhou
rulers.note: Ma Zhan'ao page: 'defected to the Qing Dynasty in 1872'; the page gives no start date (Dungan page: movement in Gansu in 1862).

rulers.name: Ma Guiyuan
rulers.title: Hui commander at Xining
rulers.note: Dungan page: launched a movement in Gansu in 1862; captured when Xining fell in late 1872.

rulers.name: Ma Wenlu
rulers.title: Hui commander at Suzhou (Jiuquan)
rulers.note: Dungan page: launched a movement in Gansu in 1862; 'The city was under the command of Ma Wenlu' when it fell on 24 October 1873.

correction.text: the Hui centres of 1862: the Xi'an siege, Jinjipu, Hezhou, Xining and Suzhou

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Dungan row. 'By late June 1862, organized Muslim bands laid siege to Xi'an'; Ma Zhan'ao, Ma Guiyuan and Ma Wenlu launched movements in Gansu in 1862 and Ma Hualong rose at Jinjibao (no dates). The pages tie each leader to a city only through the later sieges (Hezhou, Xining, Suzhou, Jinjipu), so five radii stand for the first year's centres; no boundary is on any page. No infobox area.

union.text: Ma Hualong's domain: 'roughly today's Ningxia' (Ma Hualong page), with Guyuan and Ningxia Prefecture

correction.text: the Hui zone of 1863: Ningxia, Pingliang, the Xi'an siege, Hezhou, Xining and Suzhou

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In January 1863, Hui forces captured Guyuan', 'In August 1863, Hui forces captured Pingliang Prefecture', 'In October 1863, Hui forces captured Ningxia Prefecture' and Ma Hualong's forces attacked Lingzhou. The Ma Hualong page gives his 'direct influence' as 'roughly today's Ningxia and easternmost Gansu', which stands for the Ningxia-Guyuan-Pingliang block; the Xi'an siege and the three western centres continue.

correction.text: the Hui zone of 1864-1868: Ningxia, Pingliang, Xi'an siege, Hezhou, Weiyuan, Xining, Suzhou and Urumchi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In February 1864, Hui forces captured Weiyuan County' (the page's Gansu list; the county town is placed by the researcher) and 'On October 3, 1864, the Manchu fortress of Ürümqi also fell to the joint forces of Ürümqi and Kuchean rebels'. A 100 km radius round Urumqi stands for the Dungan state there. Kucha, Yarkand, Kashgar and Ili rose in 1864 and went to the Yettishar and Ili Sultanate dossiers, not drawn here.

correction.text: the Hui zone of 1869-1870 after the retreat from Shaanxi: Ningxia, Pingliang, Hezhou, Weiyuan, Xining, Suzhou and Urumchi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the Hui rebels in Shaanxi fled to Gansu in 1869' after Zuo Zongtang had beaten the Nian in the province by 1868; the Xi'an ring is dropped. The page adds that Xi'an 'withstood a rebel siege for two year in 1870 and 1871' without naming the besiegers; read as raiders from Gansu, so no land is added.

correction.text: the Hui zone of 1871: Hezhou, Weiyuan, Xining, Suzhou and Urumchi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Ma Hualong surrendered in January 1871' and the Ningxia domain ('roughly today's Ningxia and easternmost Gansu') returned to the Qing. The pages do not say when Pingliang, Guyuan or Weiyuan were retaken; Pingliang is dropped with Ma Hualong's block, Weiyuan kept with Hezhou.

correction.text: the Hui zone of 1872: Suzhou and Urumchi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Ma Zhan'ao 'defected to the Qing Dynasty in 1872' (Hezhou) and 'Xining fell after a three-month siege in late 1872'. Weiyuan is dropped with Hezhou (the page does not say).

correction.text: Urumchi, the Dungan state in Xinjiang, 1873-1875

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Zuo Zongtang laid siege to Suzhou in September 1873 with 15,000 troops'; 'the city fell on October 24'. The Dungan state in Xinjiang is left at Urumchi until the Qing 'appeared at Urumchi' in August 1876 (Qing reconquest page).

correction.text: Manas and the belt of towns north of Urumchi, the last Dungan stand, to 6 November 1876

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Urumchi 'soon surrendered' in August 1876 (a footnote dates the fall to 18 August); a footnote quoting Fairbank says 'In a belt of towns north of Urumchi, the Sinkiang Tungans made their last stand as a cohesive group'; the Qing began the siege of Manas on 2 September 1876 and 'on 6 November it surrendered'. The page does not say who held Manas.

region.text: Jinjipu (Jinjibao), the Jahriyya headquarters, 'a few kilometers south from today's Wuzhong City'

ledger.note: 1862: Ma Hualong rises at Jinjipu ('from the beginning of the anti-Qing Muslim Rebellion in 1862'). No day or month; the Dungan page also has Ma Hualong 'began an uprising at Jinjibao' without a date. Coordinates are the researcher's.

1862: Ma Zhan'ao launches a movement in Gansu ('no exact date given'). The page ties him to Hezhou only through the 1872 assault ('Ma Zhan'ao offered to surrender his stronghold'); the Ma Zhan'ao page is silent on when he rose or took Hezhou.
1862: Ma Guiyuan launches a movement in Gansu (no date); the page ties him to Xining through its fall in late 1872, 'its commander, Ma Guiyuan, was captured'.
1862: Ma Wenlu launches a movement in Gansu (no date); 'The city was under the command of Ma Wenlu' at its fall (October 1873). Coordinates for Jiuquan are the researcher's.

region.text: Xi'an, 'surrounded' by Hui forces by late June 1862

ledger.note: June 1862: the Shaanxi rising. Zhang Fu was seized at Youfang Street, Lintong, on 2-3 June 1862 and executed on 9 June (the same page elsewhere says 'May 1862'); 'By late June 1862, organized Muslim bands laid siege to Xi'an'. The rising spread 'in the spring of 1862' as Taiping troops approached southeast Shaanxi, though rumours of Hui aid to the Taiping were 'false, as it turned out'. The page does not say the rebels held ground, only the siege.
January 1863: 'In January 1863, Hui forces captured Guyuan.' Coordinates are the researcher's.
August 1863: 'In August 1863, Hui forces captured Pingliang Prefecture.'

region.text: Ningxia Prefecture and the Yellow River plain round Jinjipu

ledger.note: October 1863: 'In October 1863, Hui forces captured Ningxia Prefecture' and 'the same month, Ma Hualong's forces attacked Lingzhou' (Qing accounts have them capture it and kill more than 20,000). The Ma Hualong page gives his direct influence as 'roughly today's Ningxia and easternmost Gansu'; the whole Ningxia region is the researcher's stand-in for the prefecture and Lingzhou.

February 1864: 'In February 1864, Hui forces captured Weiyuan County.' The page's list is the Ningxia and Gansu campaign of 1863-1864; the page does not name the province of this Weiyuan, so the Gansu county is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Manchu fortress of Urumchi (Urumqi) and its district

ledger.note: 3 October 1864: 'On October 3, 1864, the Manchu fortress of Ürümqi also fell to the joint forces of Ürümqi and Kuchean rebels' (the Urumqi rebellion began 26 June 1864). The 100 km radius is a stand-in.

region.text: the Hui rebels' ground in Shaanxi, left in 1869

ledger.note: 1869: 'the Hui rebels in Shaanxi fled to Gansu in 1869' after Zuo Zongtang, sent in 1867 and made governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu in 1866, 'defeated the Nian in the province by 1868'. The page does not say which Shaanxi places the Hui held; Xi'an is the only one named.

region.text: Jinjipu and Ma Hualong's domain, Ningxia and easternmost Gansu

ledger.note: January 1871: 'Ma Hualong surrendered in January 1871' after the siege of Jinjipu (Dungan page: began September 1870, 'sixteen-month siege'; Ma Hualong page: besieged from July 1869, a year inferred by its footnote, which fits the sixteen months better). A massacre followed (over a thousand dead). The pages do not say when Pingliang, Guyuan and Lingzhou were retaken; they are folded into this loss.

region.text: Hezhou and the Weiyuan county seat

ledger.note: 1872: Zuo's 1872 assault on Hezhou was repulsed; then Ma Zhan'ao 'offered to surrender his stronghold' and, per the Ma Zhan'ao page, 'was defected to the Qing Dynasty in 1872' (no month, no place on the Ma Zhan'ao page). Weiyuan is folded in by the researcher; no page says it fell with Hezhou.
Late 1872: 'Xining fell after a three-month siege in late 1872'; Liu Jintang's campaign began in August 1872 and Ma Guiyuan was captured.
24 October 1873: 'Zuo Zongtang laid siege to Suzhou in September 1873 with 15,000 troops'; 'the city fell on October 24' under Ma Wenlu's command.

region.text: Urumchi, which 'soon surrendered' to the Qing

ledger.note: August 1876: the Qing 'appeared at Urumchi' and 'the place soon surrendered and the garrison was massacred'; a footnote dates the fall to 18 August. The Qing page does not name the holder; that it was the Dungan state comes from the Dungan page (rebels took it in 1864; 'Tuo Ming's Dungan forces were defeated at the Battle of Urumqi (1870)'; the page does not say who held it afterward) and from the Fairbank footnote on the 'Sinkiang Tungans' north of Urumchi.

6 November 1876: the Qing began the siege of Manas on 2 September 1876 and 'on 6 November it surrendered'; the garrison was slaughtered. The page is silent on who held Manas; it sits in the belt of towns 'north of Urumchi' where, per a Fairbank footnote, the 'Sinkiang Tungans made their last stand as a cohesive group'.

region.text: the last Dungan towns in Xinjiang

ledger.note: November 1876 is the researcher's end of Dungan-held land. The Dungan page dates the war to 1862-1877 and gives no end-event of its own; its Xinjiang section stops mid-sentence. 17 December 1877 (Kashgar, Yettishar) is on the Qing reconquest page and is not Dungan land.

wars.name: Dungan Revolt
wars.outcome: Qing victory: Jinjipu fell in January 1871, Hezhou and Xining in 1872, Suzhou on 24 October 1873 and Urumchi and Manas in August-November 1876; Yaqub Beg's state fell in 1877. The revolt 'led to a population loss of 21 million'; 'Gansu lost 74.5% (14.55 million) of its population'; 'Zuo had 7,000 Hui people executed and resettled the rest in southern Gansu'.
wars.note: Yettishar (Yaqub Beg) is a belligerent only on the Xinjiang side: the Dungan page has Yaqub Beg defeat Tuo Ming's forces at Urumqi (1870).

certainty.note: The Dungan page dates sieges and captures but draws no boundaries; every region is a radius or the Ningxia region round a named town.

sources.title: Dungan Revolt (1862-1877)
sources.note: Dates for the Xi'an siege (late June 1862), Guyuan, Pingliang, Ningxia, Weiyuan (1863-1864), Urumchi (3 October 1864), Jinjipu (January 1871), Xining (late 1872), Suzhou (24 October 1873); the Hui flight to Gansu in 1869; death tolls.

sources.title: Ma Hualong
sources.note: Jahriyya leader, base at Jinjipu, 'roughly today's Ningxia and easternmost Gansu'; surrender January 1871; death 2 March 1871; siege dated July 1869 (year inferred).

sources.title: Ma Zhan'ao
sources.note: 'defected to the Qing Dynasty in 1872'; silent on when he rose and on the land held.

sources.title: Qing reconquest of Xinjiang
sources.note: Urumchi, 18 August 1876 (footnote); Manas, siege from 2 September and surrender 6 November 1876; Kashgar 17 December 1877; Fairbank footnote on the Sinkiang Tungans.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from four pages. Not settled: (1) the dossier ends in November 1876 (the last Dungan towns, on the Qing reconquest page), but the Dungan page's own span is 1862-1877 and the war entry keeps that. (2) The Jinjipu siege: the Dungan page says it began in September 1870 and lasted sixteen months, ending January 1871 (these do not add up); the Ma Hualong page says July 1869 (its footnote says the book gives no year). A September 1869 start would fit sixteen months; the dossier states January 1871 for the fall and leaves the start in the note. (3) The Zhang Fu date: June 2-3 and June 9 1862 (seizure and execution) beside a sentence 'Following Zhang Fu's death in May 1862' on the same page. (4) The Xi'an siege 'in 1870 and 1871' by unnamed rebels, after the Shaanxi Hui had fled to Gansu in 1869; no land is added for it. (5) The pages tie Ma Zhan'ao, Ma Guiyuan and Ma Wenlu to Hezhou, Xining and Suzhou only through the sieges; the 1862 gains are placed on those cities at confidence 2. (6) Tarim Basin and Ili: the Dungan page dates the Kucha rising (3-4 June 1864; Rashidin Khoja), the Yarkand rising (26 July 1864) and the Ili rising (10 November 1864; Huiyuan fell 8 January 1866), but these were absorbed into other states: Kucha and Yarkand into Yettishar (existing dossier, 1866) and Ili into the Ili Sultanate (existing dossier, 1864-1871); this dossier draws none of them. The page does not mention a Taranchi Sultanate or the Russian occupation of Ili. (7) Qinghai: the page names Xining only, not a separate Qinghai rebel state. (8) Manas: the Qing page is silent on the holder, hence confidence 1. (9) Coordinates for Jinjipu, Jiuquan (Suzhou), Guyuan, Weiyuan (Gansu) and Manas are the researcher's; the gazetteer lacks the names Jinjipu/Jinjibao, Jiuquan, Guyuan, Weiyuan and Manas. Family china-division is a pick; the colour agent may prefer another. Counterpart qing-dynasty is written by ea-08-a/b.
